examples.solution_text:
(a) The terms are like terms. Subtract the coefficients.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}8m-11m\\&=(8-11)m\\&=-3m\end{aligned}$
(b) Group the like terms, keeping each sign.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}4+7m-2m-9\\&=(7m-2m)+(4-9)\\&=5m-5\end{aligned}$

Group the $a$ terms, the $b$ terms and the constants.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}6a-3b-2a-5b+7-4\\&=(6a-2a)+(-3b-5b)+(7-4)\\&=4a-8b+3\end{aligned}$

(a) Since $qp=pq$, all three terms are like terms.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}4pq+3qp-2pq\\&=(4+3-2)pq\\&=5pq\end{aligned}$
(b) The $x^2$ terms are like terms; $8x$ is unlike them.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}3x^2+8x-7x^2\\&=(3-7)x^2+8x\\&=-4x^2+8x\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
(a) Simplify $5r+r^2-r^2-8r+4$.
(b) A student writes $2v^2+3v=5v^3$. Explain the error and give the simplified expression.
examples.solution_text:
(a) Group terms with the same pronumeral and power.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}5r+r^2-r^2-8r+4\\&=(r^2-r^2)+(5r-8r)+4\\&=0-3r+4\\&=-3r+4\end{aligned}$
(b) $v^2$ and $v$ have different powers, so the terms are unlike. Their coefficients cannot be added to make one term, and adding terms does not add powers.
The expression $2v^2+3v$ is already simplified.

examples.derivation: The signed coefficients give 8−11=−3, so part (a) is −3m. In part (b), 7−2=5 and 4−9=−5, giving 5m−5. This follows the supplied booklet's collection and sign-preservation method.
Collecting separately gives (6−2)a=4a, (−3−5)b=−8b and 7−4=3, hence 4a−8b+3. Every sign is preserved during regrouping.
Since qp=pq, part (a) has coefficient 4+3−2=5 and simplifies to 5pq. In part (b), 3−7=−4 for the squared terms; 8x remains separate, giving −4x²+8x.
In part (a), r²−r²=0 and 5r−8r=−3r, leaving −3r+4. In part (b), v² and v have different powers and are unlike terms; 2v²+3v is already simplified. Addition does not merge their powers.
